topic: 5 things you need to know: AI chatbots got voting information wrong ahead of the midterms
post:
Millions of people asked AI how to vote. A lot of the answers were wrong. 🗳️
Here are 5 things you need to know.

1️⃣ A big test
The Washington Post reviewed more than 3,000 voter guides produced by six popular AI chatbots and found significant errors.

2️⃣ Made-up races
The Post found chatbots invented races that don't exist, mixed up candidates, and cited websites with incorrect information.

3️⃣ Wrong deadlines
NPR showed an example where a chatbot (Claude) gave incorrect deadlines for registering to vote online and by mail.

4️⃣ Companies say they're fixing it
Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI and Google told NPR they're working to prevent election misinformation. The Post says many made changes after it contacted them.

5️⃣ The safest source hasn't changed
Experts quoted in the coverage say: check your official state and county election websites.

Why it matters:
This isn't just about elections. Anything local, recent or high-stakes is where AI is most likely to sound confident and be wrong. ⚠️

Practical takeaway:
For deadlines, addresses and rules, use AI to find the official source, then read the official source. 🔍

Did you use AI for anything election-related? 👇
